Gooden Backs DoW Push to Eliminate University Ties to Foreign Adversaries | Press Releases | Congressman Lance Gooden Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Press Releases Home Newsroom Press Releases Print Gooden Backs DoW Push to Eliminate University Ties to Foreign Adversaries August 19 , 2026 WASHINGTON – Congressman Lance Gooden, who has led congressional efforts to combat Chinese Communist Party espionage and intellectual property theft, applauded the Department of War (DoW) for cracking down on American universities with research and financial ties to foreign adversaries. Last year, Gooden reintroduced the Protect America’s Innovation and Economic Security from the CCP Act (H.R. 1468), which would establish a dedicated CCP Initiative within the Department of Justice to combat CCP-backed economic espionage and intellectual property theft targeting American businesses, universities, and national security. The legislation passed the House Judiciary Committee in March and is awaiting a vote on the House floor. “American universities should be developing breakthroughs that keep America ahead, not becoming breeding grounds for our adversaries' espionage operations,” said Rep. Gooden. “I applaud Secretary Hegseth and the Department of War for putting national security first and demanding answers from these 30 institutions." Gooden Calls for DOJ Probe Into Foreign Influence of U.S. AI Policy | Press Releases | Congressman Lance Gooden Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Press Releases Home Newsroom Press Releases Print Gooden Calls for DOJ Probe Into Foreign Influence of U.S. AI Policy July 24 , 2026 WASHINGTON – Congressman Lance Gooden (TX-05) sent a letter to Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche urging the Department of Justice (DOJ) to investigate foreign interference in United States artificial intelligence (AI) policy.   In the letter, Gooden cites public reporting detailing efforts by foreign actors to influence U.S. AI policy through state-backed propaganda, foreign-linked nonprofits, and obscure funding streams designed to shape public debate surrounding AI development and weaken U.S. AI leadership.   "Artificial intelligence will shape the future of our economy, national security, and global competitiveness," said Rep. Gooden. "The United States cannot allow foreign adversaries to manipulate our AI policy and compromise our leadership on this technology.”   An excerpt from the letter:   “AI is rapidly becoming a central component of our economic competitiveness and national security. To ensure American policymaking remains free from covert foreign influence, participants in policy debates should not have vested interests or undisclosed financial relationships with our nation’s adversaries. As many Americans remain concerned regarding AI development and expansion, recent public reporting raises questions about the extent to which foreign-linked entities may be shaping these debates in ways that align with the strategic interests of the People’s Republic of China (PRC).   “These recent developments indicate possible vulnerabilities in current foreign disclosure laws and raise important questions about the adequacy of existing safeguards. Gooden, Gottheimer Crack Down on Crypto Theft | Press Releases | Congressman Lance Gooden Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Press Releases Home Newsroom Press Releases Print Gooden, Gottheimer Crack Down on Crypto Theft June 11 , 2026 WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Lance Gooden (TX-05) and Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05) introduced the Federal Cryptocurrency Theft Enforcement and Coordination Act, legislation to strengthen America’s ability to prevent, investigate, and prosecute cryptocurrency theft. The bill establishes a Federal Cryptocurrency Theft Task Force within the Department of Justice, bringing together DOJ, DHS, Treasury, and federal law enforcement agencies to serve as the primary federal coordinating body for combating crypto theft and supporting victims. The bill comes in response to a surge in cryptocurrency theft and growing losses suffered by American consumers and victims around the world. According to the FBI’s 2025 Internet Crime Report , Americans reported more than $11 billion in crypto-related losses last year. “Crypto criminals are stealing billions from Americans, and Washington lacks a coordinated strategy to stop them,” said Rep. Gooden . “As digital assets shape the future of finance, this bill protects consumers, cracks down on thieves, and strengthens trust in the crypto ecosystem.” “Last year, Americans lost more than $11 billion to crypto theft and scams, and right now, victims have nowhere to turn,” said Rep. Gottheimer . “This bill brings DOJ, DHS, and Treasury together to go after these criminals, support victims, and make sure local law enforcement has the federal backup they need.
